metricOrigin: performance.now() plus Runtime.getHeapUsage() around the isolated-world stack

steadyStateBudget.reason: Idle cost of the DEFAULT feature set on a captured watch/feed page, held open and untouched, measured via CDP Performance.getMetrics (real CPU seconds, no page instrumentation). Observed across runs: script 18.6-27.0 ms/min, task 84.7-88.7 ms/min, 6 layouts and 6 style recalcs per minute, heap +364-386 KB/min. Budgets are ~2x observed: the point is to catch a runaway interval or a layout-thrash loop, not to police jitter. Tighten as the numbers settle.

history.note: Retained because the 2026-08-18 bisect against it found a REAL ~2x regression, all measured same-machine same-sitting: 3c9a5ef2 49.30 paint / 57.70 parse+init -> 86cac849 59.00/90.40 -> ab1c45a3 86.40/119.20 -> dbd9a75e 109.80/137.00 -> 103.90/134.40 at v4.63.0. Loading the 75-module foundation graph concurrently (b5c933aa) recovered a large part of it. The absolute numbers below are NOT comparable to those, which is why this reference was retired rather than kept and papered over with ever-widening allowances.

history.note: The browser version was not recorded with this reference. On Chrome 151.0.7922.138, detached commit 836e9611 measured 196.70 ms parse/init and 134.40 ms paint, while the polished tree measured 187.70 ms and 129.20 ms in the immediately following run. The changed tree was faster, so the old reference was retired as an environment mismatch rather than widened to cover a code regression.
